feature_contracts.description: Firmware can program enable, surrogate selection, mode, timeout, stale limit, bounds, and memory base registers, then read back status over the MMIO/CSR interface.
When enabled and a valid packet is formed, the transport engine emits request valid/data and accepts response valid/data using the mandated direction contract.
If validation fails or response freshness is lost, actuator validity is deasserted and the fault latch is asserted rather than substituting a fallback command.
Validated candidate commands are bounded by configured limits before reaching the actuator outputs.
Bulk history and payload storage are exposed through declared technology-neutral memory wrappers and can be addressed from firmware-controlled base fields.

top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Firmware-visible top-level controller integrating MMIO/CSR, streaming model transport, surrogate/reference evaluation, safety monitor, timeout/staleness tracking, bounded actuator command generation, and memory-mapped bulk storage control.
top_module.functionality: The top module exposes a complete firmware-controlled control plane and a streaming inference/control datapath. Firmware programs registers to configure operating bounds, timeout thresholds, and control modes; reads status, faults, and diagnostic counters; and accesses bulk history/payload storage through MMIO windows. The controller emits model requests containing packaged vehicle state, wind/airspeed context, and reference-context fields. It consumes model responses carrying surrogate outputs and quality flags, validates them against a transparent reference and safety envelope, and generates bounded actuator commands only when inputs are valid, fresh, and in-range. On invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions, the module deasserts actuator command validity, preserves the latched fault, and does not synthesize an alternate command.
responsibilities: Expose a real firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface with address, write-data, read-data, valid, write-enable, ready, and error semantics.
Implement register decode for all declared software-visible registers and fields in DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.register_contract.
Package and emit model-request transport traffic and capture model-response traffic using the mandated direction contract.
Evaluate transparent reference and physics-based surrogate outputs and compare them under bounded operating conditions.
Track stale-data age, model-response timeout, and control-loop fault conditions.
Generate bounded actuator commands only when validated; otherwise deassert validity and latch faults.
Provide MMIO access to bulk history/payload storage through technology-neutral memory wrappers.
Never create fallback commands or substitute controllers on fault conditions.
top_module.reset_behavior: On reset assertion, internal state, pending MMIO transaction state, model transaction state, stale/timeout counters, and queued actuator request state reset to a known idle condition. Actuator command validity is deasserted, status_valid is deasserted, mmio_ready is asserted only according to idle bus policy after reset release, and fault_latched is cleared only as explicitly defined by software-controlled clear semantics in the register contract; no fallback actuator command is produced during or after reset release unless separately and validly commanded.
behavior_rules: All firmware-visible registers listed in the register_contract must be decoded by the top-level MMIO engine and must not be described as inaccessible internal state.
MMIO writes update only declared writable fields; MMIO reads return the latest committed field values and status fields.
The model request output is valid only when a request packet is fully formed and the request channel is selected by control logic.
The model response ready output may be asserted only when the top is able to accept a response beat and must follow the transport handshake contract.

If a model response is stale, malformed, or fails validation against the transparent reference or safety envelope, actuator_cmd_valid shall be deasserted and fault_latched shall assert or remain asserted.
If response timeout or staleness exceeds configured limits, actuator_cmd_valid shall be deasserted and fault_latched shall assert or remain asserted.
Actuator command outputs shall remain bounded to the configured envelope; invalid conditions inhibit validity rather than substituting a fallback command.
Do not implement any fallback command, fallback register, fallback status, fallback controller, substitute command, or fallback-on-reset behavior.
Bulk storage is technology-neutral and memory-macro-backed; it is not flattened into register arrays in the digital contract.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_mmio_csr
modules.description: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO decode block that implements the complete control plane, status readback, fault latch clear semantics, configuration fields, and address decoding for the controller and memory windows.
modules.functionality: Decodes all firmware-visible CSRs and MMIO windows. Produces explicit semantic configuration outputs for controller enable, surrogate selection, timeout limits, stale-data limits, actuator bound limits, mode select, fault-clear strobe, and memory base fields. Returns readable status fields through mmio_rdata and flags invalid addresses or accesses through mmio_error.
responsibilities: Expose firmware-readable and firmware-writable configuration fields.
Provide explicit semantic outputs that other modules can consume without hidden derivation.
Bridge MMIO transaction semantics into controller configuration and storage address windows.
Reflect controller status and latched fault visibility to firmware.
modules.reset_behavior: All output configuration fields reset to a safe disabled or default state. Read data and ready/error outputs return idle-safe values as defined by the MMIO transaction contract. The module does not assert any controller command; it only decodes and exposes configuration and readback state.
behavior_rules: Every register in DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.register_contract must be represented by explicit decode logic and must map to one or more declared output fields.
No inaccessible internal state may be described as software-visible.
Fault-clear is a one-cycle semantic output to the controller and does not itself clear a fault without controller acknowledgement semantics.
MMIO errors must be reported on invalid addresses, malformed accesses, or unsupported field writes.
Readback must be deterministic and aligned to the declared register map.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_transport
modules.description: Streaming transport engine that packs request payloads for the physics-based surrogate, accepts response payloads, and exposes handshake status to the rest of the controller.
modules.functionality: Packs model request words from explicit semantic inputs and emits request valid/data using the mandated direction contract. Accepts model responses, forwards the payload to downstream logic, and reports busy/valid/stale transport state. The module does not alter command outputs directly; it only manages transport and payload staging.
responsibilities: Emit model-request valid/data outputs and receive model-request ready as input.
Receive model-response valid/data inputs and emit model-response ready as output.
Stage request payload fields from controller-prepared semantic inputs.
Capture response payloads for validation and diagnostic use.
Expose transport-busy and transport-valid indicators to the controller.
Detect response staleness relative to the configured timing policy.
modules.reset_behavior: Transport handshake outputs and internal packet staging reset to idle. No request is emitted until enabled and a valid packet is available. Response-ready follows safe acceptance policy after reset release. No fallback payload is generated.
behavior_rules: The request path must drive valid/data outputs only from explicit semantic pack inputs and control state.
The response path must only consume valid/data inputs and must not be used to drive request-side transport outputs.
Stale response detection must assert response_stale when the accepted response exceeds configured freshness limits.
Busy indication must reflect actual in-flight transaction state, not a fabricated fallback state.
Transport logic may coexist with the MMIO control plane, but it cannot replace the MMIO control plane.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_surrogate_reference
modules.description: Physics-based surrogate and transparent reference evaluator that compares NVIDIA DoMINO-style surrogate outputs against a transparent reference model, computes validation metrics, and flags out-of-envelope or inconsistent predictions.
modules.functionality: Consumes physics-surrogate response payloads and computes both surrogate-derived commands and a transparent reference command path. Compares the two outputs, reports validation results, and emits explicit command candidates for the safety/bounding stage. The module is the declared transparent reference and physics-based surrogate evaluation partition, not a fallback controller.
responsibilities: Evaluate the surrogate and reference outputs for active-aerodynamic control.
Provide explicit surrogate and reference command candidates for downstream comparison.
Flag invalid, stale, or out-of-envelope responses through validation outputs.
Respect configured actuator bounds and operating mode selection.
Keep the transparent reference separate from any bypass or fallback path.
modules.reset_behavior: All command candidates and validation outputs reset invalid or zeroed as appropriate to the safe inactive state. No actuator-valid output is produced from reset. The module does not invent a substitute command when response data are unavailable.
behavior_rules: Validation must compare surrogate-derived and transparent reference commands within configured bounds and freshness policy.
If response_stale is asserted, validation_valid must deassert and validation_error must assert or remain asserted.
No fallback command may be generated when validation fails; only invalidation and fault propagation are allowed.
Surrogate and reference outputs must be explicitly distinct semantic signals.
Operating modes select which validated candidate is eligible for downstream bounded actuation, but not a substitute controller.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_safety_bounding
modules.description: Safety envelope and actuator command bounding stage that clamps accepted commands to configured limits, inhibits validity on invalid or stale conditions, and latches fault indicators for firmware handling.
modules.functionality: Consumes validated candidate commands and produces final actuator outputs, bounded within configured limits and suppressed when invalid conditions occur. Latches faults for software handling and reports status codes. On invalid, stale, timeout, or reset conditions, validity is deasserted rather than replacing the requested command with any fallback command.
responsibilities: Bound actuator outputs to configured tilt and deflection limits.
Deassert actuator validity on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions.
Latch faults until firmware clears them through the explicit clear-fault semantic.
Provide status and fault outputs to the MMIO block for software observation.
Never substitute a fallback command or alternate controller output.
modules.reset_behavior: All actuator outputs deassert validity and reset to safe encoded values. Fault latch is cleared only to the explicit reset baseline defined by the architecture and must not produce a command. No fallback command is produced on reset.
behavior_rules: Final outputs must be bounded and only valid when validation has succeeded and no fault conditions are active.
If validation_error is asserted or if any stale/timeout indicator is active, actuator_cmd_valid shall deassert.
The module may hold the last safe bounded value internally, but it must not assert validity without a fresh accepted command.
Fault status must be latched for firmware handling and reflected back through status outputs.
No fallback-on-reset behavior is permitted.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_history_store
modules.description: Technology-neutral bulk storage controller for control history and payload snapshots, intended to be mapped by the FPGA flow to native block RAM through declared memory macros.
modules.functionality: Controls bulk history and payload memory access for diagnostic retention and traceability. Implements address/base selection and exposes read data from technology-neutral memory wrappers. No control fallback or register-array substitute is used; storage is explicitly macro-backed. Own technology-neutral synthesizable bulk storage implemented as an inferred memory suitable for native FPGA block RAM mapping. Its declared memory-facing functional ports form the complete storage interface.
responsibilities: Expose read data to firmware-facing logic and controller analytics.
Maintain technology-neutral memory mapping suitable for FPGA block RAM inference or binding.
Report simple busy indicators to prevent unsafe concurrent access.
Implement bulk storage as an inferred memory rather than a flattened bank of scalar registers.
Return stored read data through the declared functional output port.
modules.reset_behavior: Memory access control resets to idle. No data is synthesized as a fallback; stored memory contents remain implementation-defined unless written by firmware or controller flow. For inferred storage on reset, hold the declared read-data output benign without clearing stored memory contents; no alternate or flattened scalar-register storage is created.
behavior_rules: Reads return data from the declared memory macros via the technology-neutral wrapper contract.
Busy outputs only reflect access sequencing and do not substitute for control or fault status.
The history/payload memory interface is separate from actuator control and cannot override fault handling.
Infer one synthesizable unpacked memory array with synchronous access so FPGA tools can map it to block RAM.
